The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 32 ringgit, or 0.74%, to 4,301 ringgit ($1,046.47) a metric ton by the midday break. The contract has lost 2.11% so far this week. title: Singapore, China leaders welcome launch of trade deal upgrade talks
summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore’s foreign ministry said on Friday that Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed the launch of talks on upgrading their free trade deal. The upgraded deal will create opportunities for cooperation in AI and innovation, it said. Wong also conveyed Singapore’s opposition to Taiwan independence and any unilateral moves to change the status quo, it said.

title: Gold set for worst week in eight months as firm dollar, Fed hike bets weigh
summary: Gold prices slipped on Friday and were headed for their worst week in eight months, as a resilient US dollar and expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in December weighed on bullion. Spot gold fell 2.7% to $3,525.25 per ounce by 0504 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. Bullion was down about 9.2% so far this week, its sharpest weekly decline since the week ending March 20. title: Three killed in missile strikes on Kyiv, mayor says, in biggest attack on bridges
summary: KYIV: A Russian ballistic missile attack hit three bridges on Kyiv’s Dnipro River and killed three people, the city’s mayor said on Friday, in the biggest strikes on routes connecting the left and right banks of Ukraine’s capital since the start of the war.
